content.text: Intent

A register of legal entities — organisations with legal personality that FCY deals with or references — so that other records can point at one canonical row instead of a free-text name. Each legal entity has a name and a list of entity identifiers (an LEI, a BIC, a RED code and so on), following the CDM
LegalEntity

type. It adds one thing CDM lacks: a status (draft | active | retired) so that an entity that is no longer used stays on record but is no longer offered for new business. The LEI (Legal Entity Identifier, a 20-character alphanumeric code) is optional, but when present it is well-formed and belongs to one legal entity only.
Scope
IN: a register of legal entities with name, entity identifiers and status.
IN: the LEI rules — 20 alphanumeric characters, unique across the register — and the exclusion of retired entities from selection for new business.
IN: one screen to browse and maintain the register.
OUT: the counterparty record. FCY standing rule R7 (company corpus) identifies counterparties as CDM
Party
records with an LEI in
partyId
; linking a legal entity to a
Party
is not part of this spec.
OUT: contact details, persons, accounts, roles, country of incorporation and parent/group hierarchy.
OUT: LEI check-digit verification and lookup against an external LEI registry — only the format is checked.
Scenarios
None — the register is kept by creating, editing and deleting rows through its screen; no step order matters.
Requirements
R1: WHEN a legal entity is saved, the system SHALL reject the save if any of its entity identifiers of type LEI is not exactly 20 alphanumeric characters.
The length and character rule depends on the identifier's type, so the field table cannot carry it.
P1: The system SHALL hold each LEI value at most once across the entity identifiers of type LEI of all legal entities, including within one legal entity.

R2: WHILE a legal entity's status is retired, the system SHALL leave it out of the legal entities offered when a record picks one for a new reference, while references already made to it stay unchanged.
Draft and active legal entities are both offered; only retired ones are excluded.

Constraints
Considered, none apply beyond the platform's own rules: authorization, performance, volume, availability, audit, privacy and retention, locale, cost.
Acceptance criteria
A1 (verifies R1): WHEN a legal entity is saved with an identifier of type LEI, the system SHALL accept the save only if the value is exactly 20 alphanumeric characters.
"ABCDEFGHIJ0123456789" (20 characters) is accepted.
"ABC123" (6 characters) is rejected.
"ABCDEFGHIJ01234567890" (21 characters) is rejected.
"ABCDEFGHIJ-123456789" (20 characters including a hyphen) is rejected.
A2 (verifies P1): WHEN a legal entity is saved with an LEI that another legal entity already carries, the system SHALL reject the save.
Re-saving a legal entity unchanged with its own LEI is accepted.
A legal entity carrying the same LEI value twice in its own identifier list is rejected.

A3 (verifies R2): WHEN a legal entity's status is set to retired, the system SHALL no longer list it among the legal entities offered for a new reference, while draft and active legal entities are still listed.
A record that already references the retired legal entity still shows that reference unchanged.
Migration & compatibility
None — a new entity, so there are no existing rows, users or callers to migrate.
